question: Can intervention data support discovery of causal functions that are NOT members of the predefined XOR family, including majority, mux and random essential-three-input Boolean rules?

source.train_policy: Three independently shuffled complete 32-action rounds; first two rounds fit, third validates. All arms receive identical action/consequence records.
source.held_policy: Enumerate all 32 actions with disjoint noise domain; no held updates.
source.noise: 0.05 deterministic-output flip, independent fair noise for independent family
source.truth: majority3, mux3 (one selector and two data bits), or randomly generated essential three-parent Boolean truth table (uniform among essential tables); XOR parity, pair, unary and independent controls. Hidden parent IDs, truth table, operator labels never accessible to learners.

methods.generic: Fit arbitrary conditional probability table on any 1/2/3-input mask, independent Laplace Beta(1,1) cell smoothing; neither operator names nor teacher responses supplied.
methods.selection: For each mask calculate leave-one-out Brier on first64 fit, add complexity penalty 0.003*2^order. Choose best lower-order unary/pair mask. If its raw LOO Brier >=0.09, synthesize the 10 triple masks by disjoint unary/pair union and select a triple only if it wins penalized risk. Validate proposed triple on third 32-action training round: advantage over best lower-order >=0.025 Brier and absolute validation Brier <=0.18. Otherwise use lower-order. Validate low-order against Laplace marginal null: improvement >=0.02 and Brier <=0.19, otherwise null. Refit selected mask on all96 training records.

arms.adaptive: As described. Only evaluate third-order masks when fit residual criterion triggers.
arms.fixed_full: Same candidate selection and validation, BUT always evaluate all 10 third-order fit masks; discard high-order scores unless the exact same criterion triggers. Intended same predictions, higher counted feature work.
arms.truncated: Only 1/2 input masks and null. Same selection and validation.
arms.flat: Direct 32-action Laplace frequency table from all 96 training records.
arms.parity_only: Gate16 signed Walsh parity-mask inference with its frozen fit/validation gates; no arbitrary truth-table representation.
arms.bayes: Exact integrated Beta(1,1) model evidence over null +25 1/2/3 input masks; equal prior mass 1/4 per model order. Bayesian mixture conditional forecast from all96 training records. All arms can persist the same 388 bytes of raw records, but Bayesian computes more.

methods.capacity: 2 contexts x [96 (action,label) uint8 pairs + route mask uint8 + status uint8] = 388 bytes per model. Raw records retain all fit labels; model scratch computation, process RAM, and source code excluded.
methods.metrics: Held Brier, exact three-parent recovery, false installed third-order masks, paired seed 95% approximate CI, comparison counts, exact prediction restoration after 388-byte pack, strongest-baseline deficits. No native checkpoint continuation claim.

interpretation: Always disclose each failed target. Nonlinear representation advantage over parity-only does not prove unique self-assembly if matched fixed ties, nor strong general causal transfer if matched Bayes or flat is better. Scientific native PASS requires later separate owner-authorized first-use and independent conventional baselines.
